introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the substitution $xy = v$, where $v$ is a function of $x$, to transform the differential equation
$$x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx} + xy = 2\left(x^{2}y^{2} + 1\right)$$
into a differential equation involving $v$ and $x$ only. (2 marks)

Hence, find the general solution of this differential equation in terms of $x$ and $y$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Transforming the equation.** With $v = xy$, the product rule gives
$$\frac{dv}{dx} = y + x\frac{dy}{dx} \quad\Rightarrow\quad x\frac{dv}{dx} = xy + x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}.$$
The left-hand side of the given equation is exactly $xy + x^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$, and the right-hand side is $2(x^{2}y^{2}+1) = 2(v^{2}+1)$. Hence
$$x\frac{dv}{dx} = 2\left(v^{2} + 1\right),$$
which involves only $v$ and $x$.

**Solving it.** The variables separate (for $x \neq 0$):
$$\int \frac{dv}{1 + v^{2}} = \int \frac{2}{x}\,dx \quad\Rightarrow\quad \tan^{-1} v = 2\ln|x| + C,$$
where $C$ is an arbitrary constant. Since $v = xy$, the general solution is
$$\tan^{-1}(xy) = 2\ln|x| + C \quad\text{i.e.}\quad y = \frac{1}{x}\tan\left(2\ln|x| + C\right).$$

(Check: $y = \dfrac{\tan(2\ln x + C)}{x}$ gives $xy = \tan(2\ln x + C)$, so $x\,\dfrac{d(xy)}{dx} = 2\sec^{2}(2\ln x + C) = 2(1 + (xy)^{2})$, as required.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $A\cos 4x + B\sin 4x$ is a particular solution of the differential equation
$$\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 9y = 14\sin 4x,$$
find the values of the real constants $A$ and $B$. (2 marks)

Hence, find the general solution of the differential equation. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Finding $A$ and $B$.** Let $y_p = A\cos 4x + B\sin 4x$. Then
$$y_p'' = -16A\cos 4x - 16B\sin 4x,$$
so
$$y_p'' + 9y_p = -7A\cos 4x - 7B\sin 4x.$$
This must equal $14\sin 4x$ for all $x$. Comparing coefficients of $\cos 4x$ and $\sin 4x$:
$$-7A = 0 \Rightarrow A = 0, \qquad -7B = 14 \Rightarrow B = -2.$$
So the particular solution is $y_p = -2\sin 4x$.

**General solution.** The complementary function solves $y'' + 9y = 0$. The auxiliary equation $m^{2} + 9 = 0$ has roots $m = \pm 3i$, so
$$y_c = \alpha\cos 3x + \beta\sin 3x \qquad (\alpha, \beta \text{ arbitrary constants}).$$
The general solution is $y = y_c + y_p$:
$$\boxed{y = \alpha\cos 3x + \beta\sin 3x - 2\sin 4x}.$$
